prerequisites: Having taken the first-year course 'Manufacturing Technology'
Mathematical knowledge acquired in the initial years of the degree
Knowledge of fundamental magnitudes: Dimensional, force, flow, pressure, power, electrical, etc.
Basic PC skills (word processor, spreadsheet, file manipulation, etc.)

learning_outcomes.text: Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology and quality control.
Machining of parts, basic use of machine tools and programming of numerical control (NC) machines.
Quality Control, Metrology and Industrial Property.
Acquire general knowledge of manufacturing processes and the machines involved.
Know the relationships and material flow between different manufacturing processes.
Be able to program oxy-fuel cutting machines using specific software, and operate these machines.
Be able to program numerical control (CNC) machine tools.
Be able to generate reports correctly using appropriate software, combining word processors and specific data/graphics programs.
Be able to access information sources available on the network and databases.
Be able to communicate and send information over the network.
Be able to work in a group, with respect for others, planning and completing tasks in a timely and correct manner.

syllabus_topics: Topic 3. Programming of Machine-Tools Using Numerical Code
Topic 4. Programming of Machine-Tools Using Simulators and CAD/CAM Programs. Analysis of Component Manufacturability
Topic 5. Introduction to High-Speed and High-Precision Machining
Topic 10. Introduction to Metrology and Quality Control
Practice 2. Programming and Operation of CNC Machine-Tools
teaching_methods: Online monitoring of weekly student work
Introduction to the use of Winunisoft software (editing and simulation of G code for CNC lathe and milling machine)
Online availability of Winunisoft software (editing and simulation of G code for CNC lathe and milling machine)

assessment_methods.method: Virtual Activities T1 and T2 (Theory Part)
Virtual Activities T3 and T4 (Theory Part)
Virtual Activities P1.a and P1.b (Practical Part)

assessment_rules: The student must independently pass the theoretical part (30%) and the practical part (70%). For the theoretical part, the official in-person exam (80% of theory) must be passed. If all virtual activities (20% of theory) are not submitted or average less than 5 points, a 100% theory exam must be passed. For the practical part, the official in-person exam (60% of practical) must be passed. If all virtual activities (40% of practical) are not submitted, or average less than 5 points, or if activity P2 is less than 5 points, a 100% practical exam must be passed. Detection of plagiarism or AI use in any activity results in a zero for all activities. Students opting for the December (or single final evaluation) call will take all exams equivalent to a student who did not complete any activities.
